header:
Date: 2026-10-13
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Laura Simmons (Oceancrest - Head of Security), Raj Patel (Oceancrest - Platform), Sofia Mendes (Oceancrest - CTO)
summary: Discovery focused on Oceancrest's security requirements for LLM inference. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logging, encryption (KMS/HSM), and data retention/residency. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; leaning towards Dedicated for predictable isolation but wants clarity on audit logs, key management, and on-prem options.
topics: Encryption at rest / KMS integration / HSM options
Data retention, purge policies, and residency
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:08] Laura Simmons: Hi, Laura here, head of security at Oceancrest.
[00:11] Raj Patel: Raj, platform eng, I run infra and deployments.
[00:14] Sofia Mendes: Sofia, CTO, I'll be listening in for architecture implications.
[00:18] Ethan Park: Ethan, SE at Redwood, I can dig into the technical bits.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great — agenda: run through security posture questions, what evidence you need (SOC2/ISO), SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Then we can map Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private to your requirements.
[00:40] Laura Simmons: Perfect. Quick background: Oceancrest processes PHI-adjacent telemetry in some regions, and we have enterprise customers that require SOC2 + ISO evidence. We're evaluating Redwood for an internal assistant and some API-driven features.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Understood. On SOC 2 and ISO, we have redwood internal wording — we maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 — I will share the report, there are scoped controls around change management, segmentation, and incident response.
[01:07] Laura Simmons: When you say share, is that a full report or a summary? We typically need the full Type II with auditor letter.
[01:13] Maya Chen: We can provide the auditor's report and the SOC2 cover letter under an NDA — I'll drop the package. That's standard.
[01:20] Raj Patel: For Dedicated options — we need clarity about network isolation and whether logs are accessible to us. If we're on a reserved pool, can we ingest audit logs into our SIEM?
[01:31] Ethan Park: Yes — Dedicated exposes audit logs and request-level traces. You can stream logs to your customer's S3 or to a syslog endpoint, or we can ship via a secure collector. There's also a per-token cost breakdown, but we keep separate logs per customer.
[01:46] Raj Patel: Are those logs redacted automatically? We are worried about PII in the payloads.
[01:52] Ethan Park: Good question. We do configurable masking and can enable automated redaction for common PII patterns, but for PHI we recommend you run a preprocessing filter. Also we support KV cache policies and prefix caching — sorry, not cache — KV cache is internal, but we can set retention policies that avoid storing inputs beyond a short TTL.
[02:14] Laura Simmons: That TTL — what's default? And can we set retention to zero for certain routes?
[02:19] Ethan Park: Default is 30 days for some analytics/logging, but for request bodies you can set retention to zero on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has stricter defaults but we have HIPAA-friendly configs for enterprise.
[02:34] Sofia Mendes: On encryption — we need bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS and HSM backed keys. Does Redwood support that for Dedicated or Private?
[02:44] Maya Chen: For Private deployments you can plug in your KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) — Redwood's control plane will use envelope encryption. For Hosted we manage keys but we can offer a BYOK path for enterprise customers with extra controls.
[03:00] Laura Simmons: Can you do HSM-backed attestation? Our auditors ask for HSM usage on some key ops.
[03:06] Ethan Park: Yes — with Dedicated you can use HSM-backed KMS in your cloud account and we integrate via the KMS APIs. For Private on-prem you control the HSM. For Hosted there is an option but it's negotiable under enterprise contract.
[03:18] Raj Patel: SSO — we use SAML with SCIM for provisioning. We need RBAC mapped to our teams and SSO for the admin console.
[03:25] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; you can map your IdP groups into roles. Our RBAC is role-based with custom roles for route access, model access, and admin functions.
[03:36] Laura Simmons: Are there audit logs for admin actions — like who rotated keys or changed routing policies?
[03:41] Ethan Park: Yes, all console actions, API key creation, role changes, and key rotation are logged and can be forwarded. The logs include user, action, timestamp, and request id.
[03:50] Sofia Mendes: How tamper-proof are the logs? Our compliance team wants immutable logs or export to our own S3 with Object Lock.
[03:58] Maya Chen: You can forward logs to your S3 with Object Lock enabled on your side; Redwood also offers append-only logs in the platform and writes to WORM storage for retention if required. We'll share the audit log architecture doc.
[04:12] Raj Patel: Data residency — we need inference processing to stay in EU for EU customers. Does Redwood support regional guardrails and routing?
[04:20] Ethan Park: Yes, smart routing can keep requests in a region. For Hosted we have EU regions; for Dedicated and Private you can deploy in your region or use a dedicated region in our infra. We can pin model variants to region/zone.
[04:35] Laura Simmons: On encryption in transit and at rest, I assume TLS everywhere? Any client-side encryption for payloads?
[04:41] Maya Chen: TLS 1.2+ in transit. For additional control you can use client-side encryption — encrypt payloads before sending — but that limits model utility. We also support mutual TLS for private endpoints.
[04:55] Raj Patel: How about network egress — do you allow restricting outbound calls from the runtime?
[05:00] Ethan Park: Yes, in Dedicated/Private you can restrict outbound egress. Hosted has managed network egress, but we can restrict external calls and only allow specific destinations under enterprise terms.
[05:12] Maya Chen: Quick pause — any deal blockers we should surface now?
[05:16] Laura Simmons: Key ones: need SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 summary, BYOK/HSM story, audit log immutability/export, and SAML + SCIM provisioning integration details. Also need data retention guarantees and deletion workflows for customer data.
[05:31] Ethan Park: Noted. For deletion workflows we have a data lifecycle API — you can purge datasets and we provide an attestable deletion path for Dedicated and Private. Hosted deletion is within our retention SLA but we can provide attestations under contract.
[05:48] Raj Patel: Can you walk us through a typical Dedicated network layout — VPC, subnets, NAT, etc? We need to compare to our security baseline.
[05:56] Ethan Park: Sure — normally Dedicated runs in a customer-dedicated VPC peered to Redwood control plane; compute nodes live in private subnets with no public IPs, NAT via managed egress gateways, and optional private link for admin plane. We can share a diagram after the call.
[06:12] Sofia Mendes: How does model version pinning work with rollouts? We need canary controls and automatic fallback if latency degrades.
[06:19] Ethan Park: Rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic fallback and health checks. For Dedicated you have pins per route and circuit breakers; observability hooks report token-level latency so you can implement auto rollback.
[06:33] Laura Simmons: About encryption keys lifecycle — who rotates keys and how frequently?
[06:38] Maya Chen: Customers own rotation when using BYOK; we recommend quarterly rotation but follow your org policy. If Redwood-managed keys are used we rotate keys per best-practices and provide rotation logs.
[06:51] Raj Patel: Is there a hardware isolation option — like dedicated GPU hosts that are single-tenant?
[06:57] Ethan Park: Dedicated pools can be single-tenant if required; that is a contract/ops configuration. Private on-prem obviously gives full hardware control.
[07:05] Sofia Mendes: For compliance, will Redwood sign a DPA with our data processing terms and do you support specific contractual clauses for EU data transfer?
[07:13] Maya Chen: Yes — we have a standard DPA and can add SCCs or UK addendum. For enterprise deals we work with legal to include specific clauses.
[07:22] Laura Simmons: Can you provide us with the pen test summary and remediation timeline if any findings exist?
[07:28] Ethan Park: We run quarterly pentests and can provide an executive summary; full detailed reports require an NDA.
[07:35] Raj Patel: Any story on secrets management and where API keys live?
[07:40] Ethan Park: API keys are stored in our secrets store with KMS envelope encryption; for Dedicated/Private you can route secrets through your vault (HashiCorp, AWS Secrets Manager). We support ephemeral tokens via short TTLs.
[07:54] Laura Simmons: For RBAC, can we create scoped service accounts for infra jobs with limited permissions?
[07:59] Maya Chen: Yes — we support service accounts with fine-grained roles and token scoping by route and model.
[08:08] Sofia Mendes: A practical question — if we start on Hosted to move fast and later migrate to Dedicated, how disruptive is that?
[08:14] Ethan Park: The API and SDK are the same; migration mostly involves provisioning Dedicated pool, changing endpoint URL or routing policy, and pinning models. We provide migration guides and can do blue/green migrations.
[08:28] Raj Patel: For the logging — we need request-level logs but with redaction at rest, and the ability to replay logs to reproduce incidents.
[08:36] Ethan Park: We keep full request traces for a configurable window; redaction can be applied at ingestion or on export. Replays are supported in Dedicated by rehydrating cached prefixes if retained.
[08:50] Laura Simmons: What's the SLA for Dedicated latency and uptime?
[08:55] Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and target p50/p95 latency claims per instance type; we can share the SLA doc.
[09:04] Sofia Mendes: Are there known limitations around model quantization and determinism that affect auditability?
[09:10] Ethan Park: Quantization can introduce small variance, but we offer model provenance and deterministic seeds where possible for reproducibility in evals. We'll add that to the deep dive.
[09:24] Raj Patel: On-network proofs — do you provide signed attestations for code images or runtime hashes?
[09:30] Ethan Park: We provide image signing and runtime integrity checks; attestations can be provided for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can provide attestations depending on configuration.
[09:43] Laura Simmons: For retention, auditor wants explicit deletion workflows and attestations when data is purged after a customer requests deletion.
[09:51] Maya Chen: We have a documented deletion API and we can provide a signed attestation that data for the tenant was deleted — for Dedicated/Private this is straightforward; for Hosted we provide deletion proofs under contract.
[10:05] Sofia Mendes: Any blockers for us doing a POC? We need to run sample traffic through a Dedicated pool and run security checks.
[10:12] Maya Chen: That's doable; typical POC steps: we provision a small Dedicated pool, run a bench with your sample workload (ideally redacted), you validate logs/keys/retention. We'll help with test harness and scripts.
[10:25] Raj Patel: For timeframe — how long to get a Dedicated POC environment?
[10:29] Ethan Park: Usually 2-3 weeks to provision and baseline, faster for simple configs. If you need on-prem it's longer.
[10:36] Laura Simmons: About identity provisioning with SCIM — can we on-board hundreds of users, and will group mapping be preserved?
[10:42] Maya Chen: Yes, SCIM scales; group-to-role mapping is preserved and you can sync periodically or on-demand.
[10:50] Raj Patel: One more question on backups — are model caches and KV caches included in backup retention?
[10:56] Ethan Park: KV cache is ephemeral and not part of backup; models and weights are managed by Redwood and we maintain backups of model artifacts. You can snapshot runtime state for troubleshooting in Dedicated.
[11:10] Sofia Mendes: If we need to show evidence to auditors, can Redwood provide control mappings to SOC2/ISO controls?
[11:16] Maya Chen: Yes, we provide control mappings and a security whitepaper that maps features to frameworks. I'll attach that.
[11:24] Laura Simmons: On breach notification timelines, what's Redwood's commitment?
[11:29] Ethan Park: Our incident response policy commits to notify customers within 72 hours for incidents with data exposure; specifics are in the DPA and incident response doc.
[11:41] Raj Patel: For private deployments, what's the typical ops handover? We need runbooks and on-call rotations.
[11:47] Maya Chen: We provide an ops runbook, on-call runbook, and training. For Private we can do co-managed or full customer-managed modes.
[11:57] Laura Simmons: Any SOC2 gap we've seen commonly with customers moving sensitive workloads?
[12:02] Ethan Park: Common gaps are around key rotation, tenant isolation in multi-tenant setups, and log retention policies. We work with customers to tighten those via Dedicated/Private configs.
[12:15] Sofia Mendes: Could you share an architecture diagram and compliance pack?
[12:18] Maya Chen: Yes — I'll send SOC2, ISO, pentest summary, audit log architecture, and the Dedicated network diagram after.
[12:27] Raj Patel: For the POC, we'll need a checklist of what to validate — auth, key mgmt, log export, retention, and performance.
[12:33] Ethan Park: We'll draft a POC checklist and benchmark scripts.
[12:37] Laura Simmons: Regarding RBAC for models — can we restrict certain high-risk models to a small team?
[12:42] Maya Chen: Absolutely — model-level access controls are supported.
[12:46] Sofia Mendes: Any recommendations for initial config? We want strong defaults.
[12:50] Ethan Park: Start with Dedicated for isolation, enable BYOK for keys, turn on redaction pipelines, forward logs to your SIEM, and set retention policies to meet your compliance window.
[12:59] Laura Simmons: That's helpful. On data deletion attestations — can we get a template?
[13:03] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include an attestation template in the security pack.
[13:08] Raj Patel: If we need to escalate to legal or privacy, who do we loop in?
[13:12] Maya Chen: I'll copy our legal and privacy contacts; we can schedule a contract/terms session if needed.
[13:18] Sofia Mendes: Budget question — does Dedicated carry a big uplift vs Hosted?
[13:22] Maya Chen: There is a premium for reserved capacity, but it gives predictable throughput and isolation. We'll share pricing ranges in the follow-up.
[13:31] Laura Simmons: Any quick wins to accelerate approval?
[13:34] Ethan Park: Providing your sample workload and agreeing to a short POC helps. Also, pre-sharing required compliance docs speeds the security review.
[13:44] Maya Chen: Alright let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[13:48] Maya Chen: Action items: I'll send SOC2/ISO and security pack; Ethan will draft POC checklist and architecture diagram; Raj will share sample workload and residency requirements.
[13:59] Laura Simmons: Sounds good — target dates noted.
[14:02] Sofia Mendes: Thanks everyone.
[14:05] Ethan Park: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive.
[14:09] Maya Chen: End.
